annotations.title: Look an Old Norse word up

description:
Look an Old Norse word up on Wiktionary and return its senses plus full
declension/conjugation tables — attested content (including the verbs'
mediopassive voice), not invented. Any form of the word works; an
inflected query is resolved to its lemma automatically via previously
cached paradigms and the result notes the resolution. With
search_language='eng' the query is an English word instead: the result
lists its per-sense Old Norse equivalents (the translations block) plus
their expanded entries. Returns Markdown plus the same result as
structuredContent matching the declared outputSchema.

Results are cached server-side; first-time queries reach the live upstream
politely and calls are rate limited — on a rate-limit error, wait a few
seconds and retry. Content is from en.wiktionary.org (CC BY-SA 4.0 —
attribute and share alike if republished).

SearchLanguage.description:
The query language. ``non`` looks an Old Norse word up directly (any of its
forms — an inflected query resolves via cached paradigms). ``eng`` searches in
reverse: the English Wiktionary page for the query word lists per-sense Old
Norse translations, and each distinct lemma is then looked up normally.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full declension/conjugation table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses (and the verbs' mediopassive voice) in ONE call, no follow-up norse_get_inflections. Set false for a cheap screen of which entries exist. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to adjust per call. For eng queries this governs the expanded Old Norse entries; the per-sense translations list itself is always returned.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). On an uncached query each table is one politely paced upstream fetch, so high values on cold queries are slow. Omit for the server default.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: The word to look up, in the language search_language names. Old Norse (default): a SINGLE Old Norse word, any form — an inflected form ('mǫnnum') is resolved to its lemma ('maðr') automatically via cached paradigms, and the result says so; diacritics are optional once a paradigm is cached ('madr' and 'mathr' both find maðr, 'monnum' finds mǫnnum). English (search_language='eng'): the English word whose Old Norse equivalents you want — multiword entries like 'apple tree' work.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language the query word is in: 'non' (default) looks the Old Norse word up directly; 'eng' finds the Old Norse equivalents of an English word (per-sense, from Wiktionary's translation tables) and returns their full entries. Glosses are in English either way.

name: norse_search

Entry.description:
One Old Norse entry on the page: the headword (page title) with one
part-of-speech section's senses.
Entry.title: Entry

InflectionHandle.description:
A structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm: feed ``entry_id`` (the page
title) + ``word_class`` (the POS section) to ``norse_get_inflections`` — or ask
``search`` to include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: Wiktionary page title — the lemma itself.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

NorseNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/etc.: case key → {singular, plural}.

Noun tables split by definiteness, folded into the key as a prefix:
'indefinite nominative', 'definite genitive'. Adjective tables split by gender
(suffixed: 'nominative feminine') and come one per declension class and degree,
folded in as a caption-derived prefix: 'strong nominative feminine',
'weak superlative accusative neuter', 'comparative dative masculine'.
``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch
on it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case key (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', …; nouns prefix the definiteness — 'indefinite nominative'; adjectives prefix the caption-derived declension class/degree and suffix the gender — 'strong nominative feminine') → its singular/plural forms, in table order.
cases.title: Cases

NorseNominalParadigm.title: NorseNominalParadigm

NorseNumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the two number forms of one case key. Forms are verbatim
normalized Old Norse; alternates stay comma-separated as Wiktionary renders
them. A number the table doesn't give (defective paradigms) is an empty
string.
NorseNumberForms.title: NorseNumberForms

NorseVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's tables are: finite cells
keyed by mood and tense → person-and-number → form, plus the non-finite forms
(infinitive and the participles). The mediopassive voice renders as its own
table and its keys carry a 'mediopassive ' prefix; active keys are bare.

finite.description: Mood and tense (lower-case: 'indicative present', 'subjunctive past', 'imperative present'; the mediopassive table's keys are prefixed — 'mediopassive indicative past') → person and number ('first singular' … 'third plural') → the form. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite form ('infinitive', 'present participle', 'past participle'; mediopassive-prefixed for that voice) → {'form': <the form>}.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

the page doesn't exist). ``found`` is False and there is no body.

One Old Norse word a translations table offers for an English sense.

what ``norse_get_inflections`` needs).

found.description: False when nothing matched. For an eng query, True means Old Norse translations were found — entries may still be empty when none of them could be expanded (see translations).

resolved_from.description: The original inflected query when resolved; else empty. non queries only — always empty for eng results.

resolved_lemma.description: The lemma actually searched when resolved; else empty. non queries only — always empty for eng results.
resolved_lemma.title: Resolved Lemma

search_method.description: How the match was found: 'direct' = the query itself matched; 'lemma_index' = an inflected form resolved via a previously cached paradigm; 'translations' = an English query resolved via Wiktionary translation tables.
